question: Separatists in Transnistria, a pro-Russian region in Moldova, have adopted a resolution calling for ‘protection’ from Russia against alleged pressure from Moldova. It is not clear exactly what they expect from Russia. Russia has responded by saying that protecting the people of Transnistria is a priority.

This situation is reminiscent of the situation in eastern Ukraine in 2022, when Russia used the protection of Russian minorities as an argument for invasion. The Moldovan authorities have dismissed the resolution as propaganda. The conflict in Transnistria arose with the collapse of the Soviet Union, when the region seceded from Moldova. This led to a brief war in 1992.
Moldova, which has a pro-European government, fears this will drag it into conflict and accuses Transnistrian factions of instigating war. 1.
What is the Vice-President / High Representative’s assessment of recent developments in Transnistria, where separatist authorities have asked Russia for ‘protection’ from Moldova?
What possible consequences does the Vice-President / High Representative see for stability in Moldova and in the region?
What role is the European Union playing to prevent a possible conflict in Transnistria?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.4.2024) The EU is following closely developments related to the Transnistrian region. The EU believes that stability in the region is in the interest of all, in particular people from both banks of the Nistru river.

The EU notes that the so-called VII Congress of all deputies organised on 28 February 2024 attracted an unprecedented media attention, sparking various speculations aimed at destabilisation of the situation. Such speculations have not materialised, and Moldovan authorities have dismissed them as disinformation and attempts to sow panic among the population.

The EU is in permanent contact with the Government of the Republic of Moldova and trusts their capacity to manage any destabilisation attempts. The EU also encourages both sides to engage in constructive dialogue.

The EU continues to support a peaceful, sustainable and comprehensive settlement of the Transnistrian conflict on the basis of respect for the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Republic of Moldova within its internationally recognised borders.
